quarterly_data.signal: Fourth-quarter 2025 results (CEO): 'Revenue grew 69%, fueled by 123% growth in E-Infrastructure Solutions and 24% growth in our Transportation Solutions. Organic growth in the quarter was 36%.' Adjusted EPS grew 78% to $3.08 and adjusted EBITDA grew 70% to $142 million. Full-year 2025: revenue growth of over 32%, adjusted diluted EPS growth of over 53%, gross margins of 23%, and adjusted EBITDA margins exceeded 20% for the first time in the company's history.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue +69%; E-Infrastructure +123%; organic 36%; adj. EPS $3.08 (+78%); adj. EBITDA $142 million (+70%); FY2025 revenue growth over 32%, adj. EPS growth over 53%

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog and visibility at year-end 2025 (CEO/CFO): signed backlog $3 billion (a 78% increase from year-end 2024, 49% excluding CEC); unsigned awards of $301 million; combined backlog $3.3 billion (up 81%, or 42% excluding CEC); a pipeline of future-phase opportunities that now exceeds $1 billion, for 'a pool of work approaching $4.5 billion'. Q4 book-to-burn was 1.64x for backlog and 0.81x for combined backlog. The CEO said the $1 billion-plus future-phase work is tied to projects Sterling is actively working on and 'the lion's share of that are with the big name hyperscalers that everybody knows' (not named).
quarterly_data.figure: signed backlog $3 billion (78%); unsigned awards $301 million; combined backlog $3.3 billion (81%); future phase exceeds $1 billion; pool approaching $4.5 billion; book-to-burn 1.64x / 0.81x

quarterly_data.signal: E-Infrastructure segment (CEO): full-year revenue grew 59% including 40% organic growth, adjusted operating income grew 67%, and adjusted operating margins reached nearly 25%. In Q4, revenue grew 123% including 67% organic growth, with 'The data center market, again, was the primary growth driver'. The Rocky Mountain site development operation, solely focused on mission-critical work, grew more than 150%. Mission-critical work (data centers, large manufacturing and semiconductor) represented 84% of E-Infrastructure signed backlog at year-end, and the aggregate of E-Infrastructure signed backlog, unsigned electrical awards and future-phase site development opportunities totaled more than $3 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: E-Infrastructure FY revenue +59% (40% organic); Q4 +123% (67% organic); adj. operating margins nearly 25%; mission-critical 84% of signed backlog; E-Infrastructure visibility more than $3 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Initial 2026 guidance (CFO/CEO): revenue of $3.05 billion to $3.2 billion; adjusted diluted EPS of $13.45 to $14.05; adjusted EBITDA of $626 million to $659 million; midpoints represent 25% revenue growth, 26% adjusted EPS growth and 28% adjusted EBITDA growth. E-Infrastructure revenue growth of 40% or higher in 2026, including 20% growth or higher in the legacy business, with adjusted operating margins in the 23% to 24% range. 2026 CapEx forecast $100 million to $110 million, with the increase driven by investments to support growth and productivity.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue $3.05 billion to $3.2 billion; adj. diluted EPS $13.45 to $14.05; adj. EBITDA $626 million to $659 million; E-Infrastructure growth 40% or higher (legacy 20% or higher); E-Infra margins 23% to 24%

quarterly_data.signal: CEC electrical business (CEO): Q4 CEC revenue increased 21% from its prior-year fourth quarter, with 'Customer demand is very strong, particularly in the Texas data center market.' Labor is the constraint: 'if I had another 1,000 electricians in Texas ... I think we could put them to work in 30 days or less.' Sterling is signing a lease that triples the size of CEC's modular build facility; the new facility is over 300,000 square feet and prefabricates everything from exterior piping and conduit around duct banks to the cabinets that go into the data centers, freeing electrician capacity and lifting margins. On combining site development with CEC in Texas, the CEO expects to 'talk about some very nice awards that take place in Texas' in the first half of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: CEC revenue +21%; 1,000 electricians could be put to work in 30 days or less; modular facility over 300,000 square feet (lease triples size)

quarterly_data.signal: Hyperscaler demand and project scale (CEO): 'we anticipate that the current strength in data center demand will continue for the foreseeable future'; working with hyperscaler customers on the next 3 to 5 years, 'We don't see anything slowing down. If anything, we continue to see it accelerate.' Projects are now 'data campuses' with multiple buildings - on one newly started Texas job 'the parking lot is 100 acres'. Sterling is being pulled into Texas ('on fire') and the Pacific Northwest, where several projects will probably be released in '27; the Northeast has early activity.

Next-generation data centers with on-site power (CEO): 'the next generation of these projects are going to have self-power generation on them', which adds underground water, utility and electrical scope for Sterling; 'Those projects really won't start getting until '27 or '28. We may see one this year'.
quarterly_data.figure: self-power-generation data center projects from '27 or '28

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor fab site work (CEO): 'I don't think we're going to see a major phase of semiconductor come on until 2030 or so', but a few projects will hit in the near future and some are 'close to shore and will be awarded in 2026'. A data center job averages about 3 years for Sterling, while the coming semiconductor plants 'will be closer to 7- to 10-year projects' whose total scope 'could approach $1 billion'. Margins on semiconductor and manufacturing site work are comparable to data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: major semiconductor phase 2030 or so; fab projects 7- to 10-year, scope could approach $1 billion
